**DonorDock** is generally the better choice if your priority is a **dedicated fundraising CRM** for donor stewardship, follow-up workflows, and relationship management.[1][2][6] **Givebutter** is usually the better fit if you want a more **all-in-one fundraising platform** with donation forms, peer-to-peer fundraising, events, ticketing, email/text tools, and a free-start pricing model.[2][3][8]

Here’s the practical difference:

| Category | DonorDock | Givebutter |
|---|---|---|
| Core focus | Donor CRM and stewardship[1][2][6] | All-in-one fundraising platform[2][3][8] |
| Best for | Managing donor relationships and follow-up workflows[1][2][7] | Running campaigns, events, and peer-to-peer fundraisers in one place[2][3][8] |
| Pricing model | Marketed as the more affordable option, with subscription-style pricing implied by comparison pages[1][3] | Free to use with a tip-or-fee model; can apply a 3% platform fee if tips are disabled[2][4] |
| Automation/workflows | Emphasizes more workflow actions and stewardship-oriented automation[1] | Includes CRM and automations, but comparison pages describe fewer available actions[1] |
| Reporting | More focused on turning reports into follow-up actions[1] | Reporting is present, but comparison pages say it is less action-oriented[1] |

If you are choosing based on **fundraising operations**, use **Givebutter** if you need events, auctions, peer-to-peer pages, and donor communications bundled together.[2][3][8] If you are choosing based on **donor management depth**, use **DonorDock** if you care most about segmentation, stewardship, follow-up tasks, and a CRM-centered workflow.[1][2][7]

A useful shortcut:

- Choose **DonorDock** if your team says, “We need better donor tracking and follow-up.”
- Choose **Givebutter** if your team says, “We need one platform to run fundraising campaigns and events.”
